title: SRE duty handoff + weekly reliability readout (scratch)
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for the 1) on-call handoff, and 2) prep notes for the weekly SRE ops sync + reliability readout. Mix of metrics to call out, oddities I noticed in paging trends, and action items to assign during the meeting. Not polished — just my brain dump before the lineup.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- System health: token-serving latency SLOs mostly stable, small regressions on tail p50->p99 for gen-1 pool over the last 72h.
- Paging: total pages last week = 38 (up 27% w/w). Noise from autoscaler flaps and a recurring NFS mount race.
- Top incidents: INC-2026-115 (autoscaler thrash), INC-2026-119 (NFS race), INC-2026-125 (model cache poisoning false positive).

Metrics to surface in readout (ask product to pull if not available in dashboard):
- SLO compliance last 7d: text-gen global p99 latency target 350ms -> 92.8% (target 99.5%)
- Error budget burn rate (14d window): hosted-api text-gen = 4.2% daily burn (est.), projected depletion in ~21 days if trend continues
- Paging breakdown: 38 total pages: infra 14, runtime 12, network 6, unknown/ops 6
- Repeat pager sources: autoscaler (9), NFS (7), KV cache invalidations (5)

Paging trend notes (observations):
- Autoscaler thrash: seen during low-traffic simulated loads (nightly canary). Scaling decisions flip between 2/8/2 nodes -> causes brief cold-starts and spikes. Root cause likely heuristics threshold + new metric with short smoothing window (PR #1723 changed smoothing to 1m).
- NFS mount race: intermittent after rolling kernel updates on a subset of nodes — mounts failing then recovering; results in 503s. Repro on a small fleet when staging patch 2026-05-18 applied.
- Model cache poisoning alert: false positives after we tightened the checksum matcher; false positives triggered eviction cascade. Need to relax rule or add TTL safeguard.

Top incidents quick notes:
- INC-2026-115 (autoscaler thrash) — timeline: 03:20-03:52 UTC 2026-05-20. Impact: increased latency p99 for gen-1 routes, minor customer error rates. Temporary mitigation: pinned canary to fixed group; long-term: revert smoothing change in PR #1723 or change to hysteresis. Owner: Miguel (follow-up: propose config change and A/B test).
- INC-2026-119 (NFS race) — timeline: rolling node kernel updates + mounts failing 06:10-06:40 UTC 2026-05-21. Impact: 503s for a subset of dedicated customers until mounts remounted. Mitigation: ensured systemd automount fallback, reapply prewarm. Owner: Priya (infra) to coordinate kernel roll back and vendor bug ticket. Linked: JIRA:OPS-3589.
- INC-2026-125 (cache alert) — timeline: 14:00-14:15 UTC 2026-05-21. Impact: transient higher cache misses, causing token regen on some requests. Mitigation: increased TTL and paused checksum strictness. Owner: Samir (runtime). Follow-up: add synthetic that simulates checksum mismatch to catch false positives.

Handoff checklist for incoming on-call (short bullet list to paste into Slack):
- Current known problems: autoscaler thrash (INC-2026-115) — stable mitigations in place; NFS mount race still active on subset, full mitigation pending; cache alert handled but watch for re-triggers.
- Where to look first: Reliability Dashboard -> SLOs (p99 latency, error rates), "Paging by source" report, infra node health (kernel version mismatch), autoscaler metrics (scale decisions log).
- Pager filters: only alerts with severity >= high, suppress noisy autoscaler flaps (we set threshold in PagerDuty filter). If unsure, ping #sre-oncall and tag Miguel/Priya.
- Escalation path: oncall -> shift lead Miguel -> eng manager Priya.

Action items (to discuss and assign in the ops sync):
- AI-1: Miguel to run retrospective on smoothing change in PR #1723 and propose tuned smoothing + hysteresis by EOD 2026-05-27. (owner: Miguel, due: 2026-05-27)
- AI-2: Priya to open vendor support ticket for kernel/NFS vendor, schedule rollback window and report to infra by 2026-05-24. (owner: Priya, due: 2026-05-24)
- AI-3: Samir to add synthetic test for checksum mismatch and add TTL fallback to cache eviction logic; small PR by 2026-05-26. (owner: Samir, due: 2026-05-26)
- AI-4: Me (Ava) to prepare short slide (2 slides) showing error budget trajectory + suggested throttle strategies for next ops sync. (owner: Ava, due: 2026-05-25)
- AI-5: Ops to review pager rules: suppress autoscaler noise and create a separate low-severity channel for flaps. (owner: oncall rotation, due: 2026-05-29)

Questions I want answered in the meeting:
- Is the nightly canary load pattern expected to trigger scaling? Should we add a 'test' label to avoid production autoscaler reactions?
- Can product tolerate a temporary p99 degradation (95% compliance) for 24–48h while we test autoscaler tuning?
- Is there appetite to invest in replacing NFS for model artifacts with an object-backed cache (S3+local prefetch)? Rough cost estimate?

Notes for the readout slides (speaker bullets):
- Slide 1: Current SLO snapshot (+ error budget projection). Call out: text-gen p99 fell to ~92.8% last 7d, burn rate accelerating.
- Slide 2: Paging trend + top sources (visual: stacked bar last 4 weeks). Call out autoscaler and NFS as repeat offenders.
- Slide 3: Top incidents this week + high-level mitigations and owners.
- Slide 4: Ask/decisions needed from leadership: approve autoscaler config A/B test; approve infra rollback window and vendor engagement; budget ok for S3-backed artifact store proof-of-concept.

Last-minute scratch reminders (things I want to check before the meeting):
- Validate that the Dashboard error budget calc uses the 7d rolling window I expect (I saw a config that used 30d in one view).
- Confirm PR #1723 stack trace and changed config keys.
- Check slack thread: #infra-updates 2026-05-21 about kernel patch.

Random notes/jotting:
- Could add optional off-ramp: if p99 < 90% for > 3h, automated fallback to cheaper but older model variant to reduce latency until resolved. Pros/cons to discuss.
- Remember to tag customers that might be impacted (account list from IA: acct-44, acct-108) before public postmortem.

End of scratch. Will clean up into a tidy readout once we agree who owns AI items in the meeting.
